notes: Summary: Enterprise insurance provider evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) for underwriting and claims automation. Heavy focus on auditable logs and customer-managed keying.

Primary ask: Full audit trail export (real-time + batch) to their SOC SIEM (Splunk HEC or S3 -> internal ingestion). Must include standardized JSON schema; no raw prompts persisted without explicit redaction rules.
Retention: Legal requires 7 years for audit logs; debug/trace logs may be retained 12 months. Immutable retention windows with ability to attest compliance.
SIEM integration options requested: HTTPS HEC with token auth, syslog over TLS, Kafka topic (TLS + SASL), or S3 bucket delivery (SSE-KMS). Prefer direct Splunk HEC for real-time alerts.

Log schema: NDJSON lines, top-level fields required: timestamp (RFC3339), request_id, tenant_id (pseudonymized), model_id + model_variant, route/path, prompt_hash (SHA256), response_token_count, latency_ms, decision_flags (e.g., fallback_used), error_code, user_role (agent/customer), source_ip (anonymized last octet), operation (generate/embeddings/rerank), storage_indicator (was_prompt_retained: boolean).

Privacy constraint: Prompts must be redacted or stored as hashed references unless explicit opt-in. Archway legal will not allow plaintext customer PII in logs. They want example redaction configs before sign-off.

KMS: Customer-managed KMS required for S3 exports and for signing tamper-evident log bundles. Support for AWS KMS and HSM-backed keys (BYOK) mandatory. Key rotation policy and proof of key separation between control plane and data plane requested.
Tamper evidence: They want HMAC or KMS-signed manifests for daily log bundles; chain-of-custody metadata and a verification endpoint for SOC to validate bundles.

Access controls: Only SOC and designated auditors may access raw audit logs; RBAC + audit of log access events required. Need ability to disable access for specific engineers and produce access history for last 2 years.
Performance: Audit logging must not add >5% p99 latency overhead to generation calls. Bulk/batched export acceptable for high-throughput jobs but real-time events required for security alerts.
Operational ask: Runbook describing log delivery retries, backfill process, and sample CI for validating schema changes. SLA: 99.9% delivery of real-time events to HEC over 30-day window.
Quote from CISO: 'We need cryptographically verifiable log bundles and proof you do not store PII by default. Show us a live export into our Splunk test tenant.'
Competitive note: They evaluated Vendor X (had poor KMS isolation) and Vendor Y (good logs but no NDJSON schema), Redwood must hit both boxes.
Risk: Legal needs confirmation of data residency for logs (US-only). Procurement will hold until legal & security sign-off (likely April decision).
